title: Grilled Flank Steak with Chimichurri
seoTitle: Grilled Flank Steak with Chimichurri | Firefighter Meal
subtitle: Bright herbs, charred beef
description: Bright herbs, charred beef. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Grilled Flank Steak with Chimichurri in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch beef. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Blend chimichurri
steps.instruction: Pulse parsley, oregano, garlic, vinegar, oil, salt, and pepper flakes until saucy but not puréed. Rest 20 minutes at room temp so vinegar mellows.

steps.title: Season the flank
steps.instruction: Pat steak dry; salt aggressively 30 minutes ahead. Grill over high heat 450°F when ready. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early. Target 145°F for steaks, 160°F for ground at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Grill and rest
steps.instruction: Grill 4–5 minutes per side to 125–130°F. Rest 8 minutes — carryover hits medium-rare. Slice thin against the grain. Hold covered at 140°F up to 20 minutes — log the time if your hall tracks food safety during long shifts. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 145°F for medium beef, 160°F for ground. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Portion and open the line
steps.instruction: Portion Grilled Flank Steak with Chimichurri onto sheet trays or hotel pans for family-style service. Stack plates, forks, and napkins at the end of the line so late-arriving crew can self-serve without bottlenecking the cook.

steps.title: Scale for larger halls
steps.instruction: When cooking for more than 8 firefighters, split into two pans halfway through so the bottom layer does not overcook while the top waits — duplicate mise en place if you double batches.

steps.title: Dress and serve
steps.instruction: Spoon chimichurri over sliced steak; serve extra sauce on the line. Hold steak loosely tented — saucing too early washes away crust.

steps.title: Final quality check before service
steps.instruction: Walk the line once before opening service for Grilled Flank Steak with Chimichurri — confirm hotel pans are labeled, backup trays are in the 200°F oven, and thermometers are calibrated. Rookies should ask a senior cook to spot-check the first portion.

proTips: Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold plates after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
Rest grilled proteins 5–8 minutes under foil before slicing — juices stay in the meat.
tonightSpread: Plate Grilled Flank Steak with Chimichurri with sides in separate pans so the crew can mix portions.
Line up Grilled Flank Steak with Chimichurri on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
Slice proteins on a cutting board at the end of the line so everyone sees the smoke ring and char.
Set sauce and pickles on the side — sauced meat holds better on the backup tray.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
Slice cold protein thin for next-day wraps or salads — faster reheat, less dry-out.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Bright herbs, charred beef. A hall pick for regular dinner nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
mealPrepNotes: Prep mise en place before the shift — Grilled Flank Steak with Chimichurri runs smoother when proteins are trimmed, spices are pre-measured, and hotel pans are labeled before the first tone.
